problem.h: They’ve got a game in their head
p: Children who love games are always inventing their own: the hero, the boss, the secret level. Most of it never leaves their head.
A blank notebook doesn’t show them how a game comes together, so the idea fizzles out.

approach.h: Fifteen pages, from big idea to the shop shelf
p: The book takes young designers through six complete games. Each one goes from the big idea all the way to the box on the shop shelf, fifteen pages at a time.
A game idea waits at the start of every game for anyone who gets stuck. The rest is up to them.

faq: Roughly six to twelve. Younger children love the heroes and pixel art, and older ones will enjoy planning levels and bosses.
Do they need a computer or console?
No. Everything happens on paper with a pencil. No screens needed.
Do they need to be good at drawing?
No. Pixel grids make characters easy, and stick figures are fine for everything else.
How is it different from The Storymaker’s Comic Book?
The Comic Book is for telling stories in panels. This one is about designing whole video games, from the hero to the box art.
